claim: A standard accelerator improves availability and directs traffic over the AWS global network to endpoints in the nearest Region to the client; a custom routing accelerator maps one or more users to a specific destination among many.
question: What is the difference between a standard accelerator and a custom routing accelerator?

values.display: directs traffic over the AWS global network
map one or more users to a specific

evidence.quote: With a standard accelerator, you can improve availability of your internet applications that are used by a global audience. With a standard accelerator, Global Accelerator directs traffic over the AWS global network to endpoints in the nearest Region to the client.
With a custom routing accelerator, you can map one or more users to a specific destination among many destinations.

claim: A network zone is an isolated unit with its own physical infrastructure, and Global Accelerator serves one static IP address per network zone, so clients can retry on the other address if one becomes unavailable.
question: How does Global Accelerator give resilience to its two static IP addresses?

values.display: a network zone is an isolated unit
client applications can retry on the healthy static

evidence.quote: Similar to an AWS Availability Zone, a network zone is an isolated unit with its own set of physical infrastructure.

Global Accelerator serves one static IP address per network zone from a unique IP subnet for each IP address family. If one address from a network zone becomes unavailable, due to IP address blocking by certain client networks or network disruptions, client applications can retry on the healthy static IP address from the other isolated network zone.

claim: Global Accelerator idle timeout periods are not customizable, and TCP keep-alive packets cannot be used to keep a connection open; you must send at least one byte of data within the timeout window.
question: Can you change the Global Accelerator idle timeout or keep a connection open with TCP keep-alive?

values.display: The idle timeout periods are not customizable
You cannot use TCP keep-alive packets to maintain

evidence.quote: If no data has been sent or received by the time that the idle timeout period elapses, Global Accelerator closes the connection. The idle timeout periods are not customizable.

To prevent connection timeout, Global Accelerator requires that you send a packet with a minimum of one byte of data, in the ingress or egress direction, within the TCP connection timeout window. You cannot use TCP keep-alive packets to maintain an open connection.

claim: Global Accelerator keeps directing established connections to an endpoint until the idle timeout is met, even if the endpoint becomes unhealthy or is removed; it picks a new endpoint only for a new connection or after an idle timeout.

values.display: continues to direct traffic for established connections

evidence.quote: Global Accelerator continues to direct traffic for established connections to an endpoint until the idle timeout is met, even if the endpoint is marked as unhealthy or if it is removed from the accelerator. Global Accelerator selects a new endpoint, if needed, only when a new connection starts or after an idle timeout.
